## Summary

Stacked on the action-configuration test branch (#16825). Adds an **execution-verification** test that proves the shared action condition engine actually **evaluates at submit**, complementing the configuration/storage coverage in the base PR.

### `tests/facility/patient/encounter/fill/fillActions.spec.ts`
Authors an encounter questionnaire (via API) with four rules over one integer answer `q_age`:
- `q_age >= 60` → senior
- `q_age < 60` → adult
- `q_age >= 18 and q_age <= 65` → working (AND)
- `q_age < 13 or q_age >= 60` → dependent (OR)

Filling age **70** makes exactly two rules hold: the **senior** and **dependent** outcome toasts fire, while **adult** and **working** do not (`toHaveCount(0)`). One submission pins every comparison operator, both connectors, and the **negative (no-fire)** case.

This is the runtime counterpart to the base PR's config test (which proves the condition compiles/stores as `patient["age"] > 60` etc.). Appointment-booking execution isn't asserted directly — it needs schedulable-resource/slot fixtures and the only registered instruction (`logging`) surfaces nothing on the appointment UI — so the shared engine is verified through the observable encounter/questionnaire path.

## Verification
- `3 passed` locally against a live backend (fresh encounter fixture).
- Type-checks clean.

Base is #16825 (`bodhi/questionnaire-actions-tests`) so it can be reviewed and merged into the test branch independently.

body.title: Add type check to CI
body.body:
> [!NOTE]
> - Follow up of #16788

Adds a `typecheck` script and runs it in the existing lint workflow on PRs to `develop`.

Nothing in CI was running `tsc`. The build transpiles via Rolldown without type checking, and `npm run build` is only invoked by the preview and Playwright workflows, so type errors could reach `develop` without failing a check. The one automated type check was `vite-plugin-checker` in the dev server, removed in #16788.

### Notes

Added to the existing `Lint Code Base` workflow rather than a new one, to reuse its `npm ci`. Runs before lint since it is faster, so failures surface sooner. CI only — not added to pre-commit hooks.

`npm run supported-browsers` runs first because `src/supportedBrowsers.ts` is generated and gitignored; without it `tsc` fails to resolve `@/supportedBrowsers`.

### Verification

Full workflow sequence run locally against current `develop`, all passing: `supported-browsers` → `typecheck` (0 errors, ~25s) → `lint` → `knip`.

Verified the generation step is required: without it, `tsc` fails with `TS2307: Cannot find module '@/supportedBrowsers'`.

body.title: [ENG-941] 🔥 Removes the unused `when` condition feature from keyboard shortcuts
body.body:
ENG-941

## The problem

The hook `useKeyboardShortcuts` read the `when` clause of each shortcut. It made a code string from the clause. Then it ran the string with `new Function()`.

Two defects were present:

1. `new Function()` runs code from a string. This is a code-injection risk. It also needs the `unsafe-eval` policy in the browser. A healthcare application must not allow this policy.
2. The old code put each condition value into the string as text. A condition value of the type string could add more code to the expression.

## The evidence

The `when` clause had the value `always` in all 108 entries of `src/config/keyboardShortcuts.json`. No other value was present.

```
$ python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('src/config/keyboardShortcuts.json'));print(sorted({s['when'] for v in d.values() for s in v}))"
['always']
```

Only that static file supplies the shortcuts. No plugin and no `care-apps` code supplies a clause. The `conditions` parameter of the hook had one purpose: to feed the `when` clause. No caller read the filtered `shortcuts` result.

So the feature was dead code.

## The fix

This pull request deletes the feature. It is better to delete dead code than to keep an evaluator for it.

The change removes:

- the `when` field from all 108 entries in `src/config/keyboardShortcuts.json`
- the `when` field from the `KeyboardShortcut` interface
- the `ShortcutConditions` interface
- the `conditions` parameter of `useKeyboardShortcuts`
- the `new Function()` call

The hook keeps the same behaviour. All shortcuts were active before, because each clause was `always`. All shortcuts stay active now.

If a shortcut needs a condition later, the team can add a typed boolean field. A string clause is not necessary.

> **Note on the history of this branch**
> The first commit added a safe evaluator to replace `new Function()`. A later check showed that the feature has no user. The second commit deletes the feature and the evaluator. The review comments on the evaluator no longer apply, because that file is gone.

## React Doctor result

Command: `npx react-doctor@latest --verbose`

Before (1 finding):

```
✖ eval() runs untrusted code strings
  react-doctor/no-eval
  src/hooks/useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:65
```

After (0 findings):

```
$ grep -c "no-eval" rd-final.txt
0
```

Errors went from 21 to 20. Warnings went from 1313 to 1312. The score went from 43 to 45.

## Tests

- `npx tsc --noEmit` shows no error.
- `npm run knip` shows no new unused export.
- ESLint and Prettier pass on the changed files.
- `npx playwright test tests/facility/patient/encounter/encounterShortcuts.spec.ts` passed. All 17 tests passed. The 9 shortcut tests show that the shortcuts still work.

## Files changed

- `src/config/keyboardShortcuts.json` — removes the `when` field from 108 entries.
- `src/hooks/useKeyboardShortcuts.ts` — removes the `when` field, the `ShortcutConditions` interface, the `conditions` parameter, and the `new Function()` call.
- `src/context/ShortcutContext.tsx` — removes the `conditions` argument.
- `src/Utils/keyboardShortcutComponents.tsx` — removes the `conditions` argument at 2 call sites.

### Proposed Changes

Fixes the **Thank You Note Generator** workflow failing on every merged PR (e.g. [run 29501202990](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/actions/runs/29501202990/job/87630447297) on #16569).

**Symptom:** The job fails at the **Checkout PR branch** step:

```
fatal: couldn't find remote ref refs/heads/QA-210-allow-qa-key-in-pr-title-jira-validation
failed to run git: exit status 128
```

**Root cause:** The workflow triggers on `pull_request_target: closed`. When a PR is merged, its head branch is typically deleted, so `checkout_pr_branch.cjs` cannot find the ref and hard-fails, aborting the job **before** the agent posts the thank-you note — defeating the workflow's entire purpose.

**Fix:** A single `continue-on-error: true` on the *Checkout PR branch* step. The checkout is not required for posting the note (the agent reads PR metadata via the API), and the downstream `checkout_pr_success` output already defaults to `'true'`, so the job proceeds and the note is posted.

```diff
       - name: Checkout PR branch
         id: checkout-pr
+        continue-on-error: true
         if: |
           github.event.pull_request
```

**Scope:** 3 lines added to the generated lock file; nothing else touched.

body.title: Consolidate agentic PR reviewers and auto-retry transient 429 failures
body.body:
## Proposed Changes

On 2026-08-20 a Copilot rate limit window failed every agentic run in this repo for 45 minutes. Nothing was actually broken: run `32344080781` was re-run by hand and attempt 2 passed. The repo has been accumulating auto-filed `[aw] ... failed` issues from these (#16731, #16732, #16705, #16706, #16670, #16708), so this PR addresses both the cost pressure that triggers the limit and the lack of automatic recovery when it is hit.

**1. Drop the Grumpy PR Reviewer, keep CARE PR Reviewer**

Two agentic reviewers fired on every `pull_request_target`, both on `claude-opus-5`, both authenticating through the same Copilot PAT. Compared head to head on the same diff (#16613) they produced roughly 40% duplicate findings at 259 vs 124 AIC.

Grumpy was the one to cut:

- It is stateless, so it re-reviewed the whole diff on every push and re-raised findings as fresh comments instead of converging. CARE tracks its own prior findings, verifies fixes at the head SHA, resolves threads, and answers @-mentions.
- Its checklist is generic (code smells, naming, duplication) and duplicates Copilot, CodeRabbit and Greptile, which already review these PRs. CARE's lenses encode actual care_fe rules (i18next keys, `query()`/`mutate()` wrappers, shadcn/CAREUI reuse, `useBreakpoints`, the `min-w-0`/`min-h-0` scroll trap, 320px viewport, 44px touch targets).
- It had no draft filter, no bot filter, no `noop` and no round cap, so it posted full reviews on lockfile-only Renovate diffs. In the 07:00 to 07:45 outage window: 7 Grumpy runs vs 1 CARE run.

Three things it genuinely did better were ported into CARE rather than lost:

- **Silent failure paths.** Its highest value finding on #16613 was two mutations with `onSuccess` and no `onError`, which CARE missed entirely. Lens 1 now checks failure handling explicitly, graded by what the user sees when a request rejects.
- **`APPROVE`.** A clean PR now gets a green check instead of a neutral comment. Safe because this is not a required check and `github-actions[bot]` cannot satisfy a required-review gate. `REQUEST_CHANGES` stays disallowed.
- **Concreteness.** The Tone section now asks for the failure and its consequence up front. The specificity, not the persona.

**2. Auto-retry runs that fail on transient inference errors**

Two layers, covering different outage lengths:

- **In-job** (`care-review.md`): the harness defaults space its four attempts only ~35s apart, so a run exhausts them in ~8 minutes, usually before a rate limit window clears. Widened to 15s/30s/60s/120s over five attempts (~12 minutes), still inside the 20 minute job timeout. Free when the model answers, since the delays only elapse on a retry path.
- **Out-of-job** (`retry-agentic-runs.yml`): a `workflow_run` watcher that re-runs failed jobs when the failure looks transient, backing off ~10 then ~20 minutes. Covers all three agentic workflows.

The classifier is the part worth reviewing closely. It is deliberately narrow in both directions and was checked against real logs:

| Test case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| The two real 2026-08-20 429 logs | transient, retries |
| Two most recent non-429 failures (real `gh pr checkout` errors) | unrecognised, does not retry |

Two non-obvious details that the first draft got wrong:

- Permanent failures must match the harness `is<X>=true` flags, **not** the bare output names. gh-aw prints `Set output 'invocation_cap_exceeded'` on every run regardless of value, so matching the bare name classified every failure as permanent, including the 429s this is meant to catch. This is also why #16742 (`exceeded daily AI credits budget`) correctly does not retry.
- Generic network strings (`socket hang up`, `ECONNRESET`) are excluded from the transient set. The MCP gateway logs `socket hang up` on its first health probe in runs that go on to succeed, so matching it would retry genuine failures containing a recovered blip.

Loop protection is `run_attempt < 3`, since a re-run emits another `workflow_run: completed` event. The watcher also skips runs superseded by a newer run on the same branch, so it never spends credits reviewing a diff that has already been replaced.

### Notes for reviewers

- `workflow_run` only fires for the copy on the default branch, so the watcher does nothing until this lands on `develop`.
- The watcher sleeps to back off, which holds a runner. Free on this public repo but not free of concurrency, which is why the delays are modest and the in-job layer absorbs short spikes without a rerun round trip.
- This treats the symptom. The root cause is that inference authenticates through a single user's `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, and Copilot rate limits are scoped per user, so every agentic run in the repo shares one person's ceiling. `permissions: copilot-requests: write` moves this to org billing and removes the shared bottleneck, but it needs an org admin to enable centralized Copilot CLI billing first, so it is deliberately not in this PR.
- There is no JIRA ticket for this work, so the PR Title JIRA Validation check is expected to fail.

ENG-953

## Proposed Changes

A new medication request must always start with an empty `dispense_status`. Only the pharmacy sets that field.

The medication request questionnaire copies `dispense_status` when the user adds a medication from an existing record. #16729 fixes this. This pull request adds the Playwright tests for the same bug.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> These tests **fail on `develop`**. They **pass** with the fix in #16729. Merge #16729 first.

### Covered add paths

The questionnaire has 7 ways to add a medication. Only 4 can copy `dispense_status`. Each test covers one path:

| Test | Path | Handler |
| --- | --- | --- |
| does not copy the dispense status of a past prescription | "Medication History" sheet → Past Prescriptions tab | `handleAddHistoricalMedications` |
| does not copy the dispense status of a single template medication | Templates sheet → one medication | `handleAddSingleMedication` |
| does not copy the dispense status when a template is applied | Templates sheet → Apply | `handleApplyTemplate` |
| does not store the dispense status in a new template | Medication actions → Add to template | `buildMedicationForTemplate` |

The other 3 paths build a fresh record, so they cannot copy the field:

- Add Medication → Medication tab (valueset search)
- Add Medication → Product tab (product knowledge)
- Medication History → Medication Statements tab (the code parses a string)

### Test method

1. Seed a dispensed medication request, or a template that holds one, through the API. The user interface cannot set `dispense_status`.
2. Drive the add path through the real user interface.
3. Submit the questionnaire.
4. Read the new records back through the API and check that `dispense_status` is empty.

Each test uses a different medication and compares the record ids before and after the flow. The tests are safe to run in parallel.

### Files

- `tests/facility/patient/encounter/structuredQuestions/medicationRequestApi.ts` — API helpers to seed and read the data.
- `tests/facility/patient/encounter/structuredQuestions/medicationRequestDispenseStatus.spec.ts` — the 4 tests.
